\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance probability under a density]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p168-b003
}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.blrAccepts}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be pointwise
nonnegative with uniform average $1$, and let $f\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$.
The derandomized BLR acceptance probability is the average over uniform $x$ of the
expectation under the density $\varphi$ of the indicator that the BLR test accepts $f$
on inputs $x,y$; equivalently, it is $\mathbb{E}_{x\text{
uniform}}\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\varphi}[\mathbf{1}_{\{\text{BLR accepts }f\text{ on
}x,y\}}]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Affine identity for density expectation]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_probabilityDensityExpectation_sub_one}
\label{FABL.two_mul_probabilityDensityExpectation_sub_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a nonnegative function on $\mathbb
F_2^n$ with uniform expectation $1$, and let $h:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$. Define the
expectation weighted by $\varphi$ by $\mathbb E_\varphi[g]=\mathbb E_x[\varphi(x)g(x)]$,
where $x$ is uniform on $\mathbb F_2^n$. Then $2\mathbb E_\varphi[h]-1=\mathbb
E_\varphi[2h-1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Centered derandomized BLR acceptance]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b004}
\label{FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.blrAccepts, FABL.convolution, FABL.convolution_apply_add, FABL.derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.signEncodedFunction, FABL.two_mul_blrIndicator_sub_one, FABL.two_mul_probabilityDensityExpectation_sub_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\phi:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ be pointwise
nonnegative with uniform mean $1$, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$. Write
$F(x)=(-1)^{f(x)}$, and define convolution by $(F*F)(y)=2^{-n}\sum_{z\in\mathbb
F_2^n}F(z)F(y-z)$. If the derandomized BLR acceptance probability is obtained by
choosing $x$ uniformly and choosing $y$ with density $\phi$ relative to the uniform
measure, then
\[2\Pr[ f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)]-1=\mathbb E_{y\sim\phi}[F(y)(F*F)(y)].\]
\end{theorem}

let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be additive, so that $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for
all $x,y$. The acceptance probability of the density-weighted BLR test for $f$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment under binary sign encoding]
\lean{FABL.mean_sq_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\label{FABL.mean_sq_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.mean}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. The mean of the
square of the function on the sign cube obtained by decoding each sign as a bit equals
the mean of $f^2$ on the binary cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment on the sign cube]
\lean{FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sq_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\label{FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sq_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.uniformLpNorm, FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sq_eq_expect_sq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional cube over $\mathbb F_2$, and
view it as a function on the sign cube through the coordinatewise bijection between
$\mathbb F_2$ and $\{\pm1\}$. The square of its uniform $L^2$ norm on the sign cube
equals the uniform average of $f(x)^2$ over the binary cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm of a self-convolution]
\lean{FABL.fourierOneNorm_binaryFunctionOnSignCube_convolution_self_eq_one}
\label{FABL.fourierOneNorm_binaryFunctionOnSignCube_convolution_self_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.convolution, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.sum_sq_vectorFourierCoeff_eq_one, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_convolution, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $f:(\mathbb F_2)^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(x)|=1$ for
every $x$. Form the normalized convolution $f*f$ on $(\mathbb F_2)^n$, and view it as a
function on the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ through the coordinatewise correspondence between
bits and signs. Its Fourier one norm, the sum of the absolute values of all its Fourier
coefficients, is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier correlation formula for derandomized acceptance]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one_eq_sum_sq_mul_correlation}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b004
}
\label{FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one_eq_sum_sq_mul_correlation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.convolution, FABL.derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_convolution, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vector_fourier_expansion}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\phi:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ be pointwise
nonnegative with uniform mean $1$, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$. Set
$F(x)=(-1)^{f(x)}$, and for $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ write $\widehat F(\gamma)=\mathbb
E_x[F(x)(-1)^{\sum_i\gamma_i x_i}]$. Then the derandomized BLR acceptance probability,
with $x$ uniform and $y$ distributed according to $\phi$ relative to uniform measure,
satisfies
\[2\Pr[f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)]-1=\sum_{\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n}\widehat F(\gamma)^2\,\mathbb E_{y\sim\phi}[F(y)(-1)^{\sum_i\gamma_i y_i}].\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on two Fourier correlations]
\lean{FABL.probabilityDensityCorrelation_add_le_one_add_bias}
\label{FABL.probabilityDensityCorrelation_add_le_one_add_bias}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.nonneg, FABL.abs_vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_mul}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\phi$ be a nonnegative density of uniform expectation one on the Boolean cube
$\mathbb F_2^n$. Suppose $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $|F(x)|=1$ for every
$x$, and every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $\phi$ has absolute value at most
$\varepsilon$. For distinct $\gamma,\eta\in\mathbb F_2^n$, the sum of the
$\phi$-weighted correlations of $F$ with the Walsh characters indexed by $\gamma$ and
$\eta$ is at most $1+\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance bound from a large Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one_le_of_half_le_sq}
\label{FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one_le_of_half_le_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.nonneg, FABL.abs_vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability, FABL.isSignValued_realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.probabilityDensityCorrelation_add_le_one_add_bias, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.sum_sq_vectorFourierCoeff_eq_one, FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one_eq_sum_sq_mul_correlation, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\phi:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ be pointwise
nonnegative with uniform mean $1$, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$. Suppose
$\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ satisfies $|\widehat\phi(\gamma)|\leq\varepsilon$ for every
nonzero $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$, where $\widehat\phi$ denotes the Fourier coefficient
with respect to the uniform measure. If some $\gamma_0\in\mathbb F_2^n$ satisfies
$\tfrac12\leq\widehat F(\gamma_0)^2$, where $F(x)=(-1)^{f(x)}$, then
\[2\Pr_{x,\ y\sim\phi}[f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)]-1\leq\varepsilon+(1-\varepsilon)\widehat F(\gamma_0)^2,\]
with $x$ uniform and $y$ drawn according to $\phi$ relative to uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distance preserved by sign encoding]
\lean{FABL.relativeHammingDist_realSignEncodedFunction}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b004

\label{FABL.relativeHammingDist_realSignEncodedFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signValue, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f,g:\\mathbb F_2^n\\to\\mathbb F_2$ be Boolean functions. Encode each output bit
$b$ by the sign $(-1)^b$, viewed as a real number. The relative Hamming distance between
the resulting real-valued functions equals the relative Hamming distance between $f$ and
$g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A fourth-moment bound by one Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.exists_vectorFourierFourthMoment_le_sq_vectorFourierCoeff}
\label{FABL.exists_vectorFourierFourthMoment_le_sq_vectorFourierCoeff}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(x)|=1$ for every $x$. Its vector Fourier
fourth moment, the sum of the fourth powers of all its vector Fourier coefficients, is
at most the square of some one of those coefficients.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine approximation from a large squared coefficient]
\lean{FABL.exists_affine_correlation_ge_sqrt_of_exists_sq_vectorFourierCoeff}
\label{FABL.exists_affine_correlation_ge_sqrt_of_exists_sq_vectorFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.affineFunction, FABL.affineSignFunction, FABL.affineSignFunction_apply, FABL.isSignValued_realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_affineFunction, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.relativeHammingDist_affineSignFunction, FABL.relativeHammingDist_realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signValue, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$, and let
$t\in\mathbb R$. Suppose some $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ has squared vector Fourier
coefficient of the real sign encoding of $f$ at least $t$. Then there are $b\in\mathbb
F_2$ and $\gamma'\in\mathbb F_2^n$ such that the uniform average of the product of the
sign encodings of $f$ and the affine function $x\mapsto b+\gamma'\cdot x$ is at least
$\sqrt t$, and their relative Hamming distance is at most $1/2-\sqrt t/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient from near-perfect acceptance]
\lean{FABL.exists_abs_vectorFourierCoeff_ge_sqrt_div_sqrt_of_near_perfect_derandomizedBLR}
\label{FABL.exists_abs_vectorFourierCoeff_ge_sqrt_div_sqrt_of_near_perfect_derandomizedBLR}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.affineFunction, FABL.affineSignFunction_apply, FABL.derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability, FABL.exists_affine_correlation_ge_sqrt_div_sqrt_of_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_eq, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_affineFunction, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one, FABL.two_mul_derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability_sub_one_le_of_half_le_sq, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb
F_2^n$, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$. Suppose $0\le\varepsilon<1$, every
nonzero frequency has vector Fourier coefficient under $\phi$ of absolute value at most
$\varepsilon$, and the derandomized BLR acceptance probability of $f$ under $\phi$ is
$1-\delta$, where $(1+\varepsilon)/2\le(1-2\delta)^2$. Then some $\gamma\in\mathbb
F_2^n$ satisfies $\sqrt{1-2\delta-\varepsilon}/\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\le
|\widehat{\operatorname{sgn}(f)}(\gamma)|$, where the coefficient is the vector Fourier
coefficient of the real sign encoding of $f$.
\end{theorem}
